transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is my sleep has gotten really messed up. Some nights I’m up half the night because my mind won’t slow down, and other times I wake up way too early and feel like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you had times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?
Yeah. There have been several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, and I still got up feeling really charged, like I didn’t even need coffee or anything.
During those times when you slept only three or four hours and still felt charged, did you also feel unusually upbeat or irritable?

Yeah, I think so. Earlier this month I felt really up, like almost lit up and unstoppable. But I was also getting irritated really easily — I snapped at my mom and even my supervisor over small questions that normally wouldn’t bother me.
During those energized times, did you feel more confident or powerful than usual?
Yeah, definitely. I remember thinking I could pay down my condo really fast, pass the CPA exams, and even start a little bookkeeping business on the side. It felt like there was no way I’d fail.
During those times when you felt unusually energized, were you more active or taking on more projects than usual?

Yeah, I was definitely doing more than usual. After work I’d come home and start cleaning, making lists for renovations, checking interest rates, and looking into side-job ideas. It was like I couldn’t shut it off.
During those times when you felt especially energized, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah. My sister actually pointed it out — I was talking really fast about stuff like equity, taxes, even paint colors, and she said she couldn’t get a word in. I could feel myself kind of pushing to keep talking.
During those energized times, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?
Yeah, they did. It was like my mind kept jumping really fast from one thing to another — mortgage payments, then CPA study plans, then kitchen cabinets — and I couldn’t slow it down enough to relax.
During those energized periods, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Not like I lost my job or anything, but it has caused problems. I’m still showing up to work, but I’ve made enough reconciliation mistakes that my supervisor pulled me aside. And at home or socially… I’ve been avoiding salsa class and seeing friends because I just don’t feel like myself.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized and lit-up period last?
The really noticeable up-and-down has been going on about a month, since the mortgage stuff became real. The charged-up part comes in stretches, but the whole cycle has been about a month.
What is the longest number of days in a row that you felt that unusually energized, lit-up way?

I’d say the longest it stayed really noticeable was part of that past month — since the mortgage became real. It wasn’t like one clean block the whole time, but the cycling between feeling charged up and then crashing has been going on about a month.
Did any one of those energized, lit-up periods last at least 4 days in a row?

I’m not totally sure if I can separate it out cleanly as exactly four days. The really obvious cycling between feeling charged up and then crashing has been going on about a month now, since the mortgage stuff became real.
During those energized periods, were you more active or taking on more projects than usual?

Yes. I was definitely doing more than usual. After work I’d get this burst of energy and start cleaning, making renovation lists, checking interest rates, even thinking up side-job ideas. It felt like I couldn’t really shut it off.
Thinking about your most energized, lit-up stretch, did it last 4 days in a row?

I can’t say for sure that one stretch was exactly 4 days straight. What I know is the really obvious back-and-forth between feeling charged up and then crashing has been going on about a month, since the mortgage became real.
During those energized times, did other people clearly notice that you were acting differently than your usual self?

Yeah, my sister noticed. She told me I was talking really fast about things like equity, taxes, and paint colors, and that she couldn’t even get a word in. I remember feeling like I had to keep going, like I couldn’t slow myself down.
Was there any stretch when that energized, lit-up state lasted 4 days in a row?

I’m not totally sure I can say it was four full days in a row. What I do know is the clear cycling between being really charged up and then crashing has been happening for about a month, since the mortgage stuff got real.
During those energized times, did you ever hear or see things that other people didn’t?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people weren’t seeing. It’s more just that I feel sped up during those times.
Have you had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?

Yeah. It’s been way more than two weeks. That depressed, guilty fog has kind of been hanging around for about five months now. It got a lot worse after I bought the condo, but it was there before that too.
During one of those energized periods, were you ever hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?
No, I haven’t been hospitalized for it. At least, not during those times or because of how I was acting.
During those energized times, did your behavior ever make it impossible for you to function normally at work or at home?

Not impossible, no. I’m still getting to work and doing the basics at home. But it has affected things. I’ve made enough reconciliation mistakes that my supervisor pulled me aside, and I’ve been avoiding salsa class and seeing friends because I just don’t feel like myself.
During those energized times, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive, like spending more money than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can’t really point to anything I did that was unusually risky or impulsive during those times. Nothing like that stands out to me.
